title: Erdős Problem #261: Reciprocal Power-of-Two Representations
description: Can every positive integer n be represented as n/2^n = Σ k/2^k over a set of distinct positive integers? Cusick proved infinitely many n work; the full conjecture remains open.

meta.author: Erdős

mathlibDependencies.description: Summation over finite sets for computing reciprocal power-of-two sums
Rational number arithmetic for exact k/2^k computations

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Previously cited axiom names have been removed from the Lean source. The 'axiomatized' status reflects that the main result is not yet fully formalized in Lean.

overview.historicalContext: Paul Erdős posed this problem in the 1970s, asking whether every positive integer n can be represented as n/2^n = Σ_{k∈S} k/2^k for a finite set S of distinct positive integers. Thomas Cusick (1989) proved the first positive result: infinitely many n admit such representations. Peter Borwein and Tamás Loring gave an explicit infinite family: for m ≥ 1, the integer n = 2^{m+1} − m − 2 is representable using the consecutive block {n+1,...,n+m}. Szabolcs Tengely, Maciej Ulas, and Jakub Zygadło computationally verified the conjecture for all n ≤ 10000, providing strong evidence for universality. Erdős also asked a deeper question: does some rational number admit continuum-many (2^{ℵ₀}) distinct infinite representations as Σ a_k/2^{a_k}? Both the universality conjecture (all n) and the continuum question remain open.
overview.problemStatement: Are there infinitely many (or all) positive integers n such that n/2^n = Σ_{k∈S} k/2^k for some finite set S of distinct positive integers with |S| ≥ 2? Additionally, does some rational admit continuum-many such representations?
overview.text: Can every positive integer n be represented as n/2^n = Σ k/2^k over a set of distinct positive integers? Cusick proved infinitely many n work; the full conjecture remains open.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization works over the rationals (ℚ) for exact arithmetic, defining recipPow2Weight(k) = k/2^k and recipPow2Sum as a Finset.sum. IsRecipPow2Rep bundles the three conditions: |S| ≥ 2, all elements positive, and the sum equals n/2^n. Known results — Cusick's infinitude theorem and the Borwein–Loring family — are fully proved (no axioms), using the partial-sum formula and explicit witnesses; the Tengely–Ulas–Zygadło computational verification is cited but not formalized. The continuum results (Part 3) are honestly-flagged placeholders: IsInfiniteRep omits the convergence condition Σ a(k)/2^{a(k)} = x, so ErdosProblem261_continuum and ErdosProblem261_two_reps are trivially satisfiable and do not formalize Part 3.
keyInsights: The weight function k/2^k peaks at k=1 (value 1/2) and decays exponentially — the total weight Σ_{k=1}^∞ k/2^k = 2, so any target n/2^n must satisfy n/2^n ≤ 2, which holds for all n ≥ 1 since n/2^n → 0

Borwein–Loring's construction n = 2^{m+1} − m − 2 uses a telescoping identity: the consecutive block {n+1,...,n+m} sums to n/2^n because each term k/2^k in a consecutive run satisfies a clean recurrence when multiplied by 2

The |S| ≥ 2 constraint excludes the trivial representation n/2^n = n/2^n (using S = {n}), forcing genuine decompositions — this is a non-triviality condition essential to making the problem interesting

The continuum theorems are honestly-flagged placeholders, not a formalization of Part 3: IsInfiniteRep omits the required convergence condition entirely, and the witness family used in the proof is even a constant function of the [0,1] parameter t — so the theorems are trivially satisfiable and do not establish continuum-many (or even two) genuinely distinct representations

Computational verification up to n = 10000 suggests universality but cannot prove it — the representations become increasingly complex for larger n, and no pattern uniform enough for a general proof has been found

sections.title: Module Header and Problem Statement
sections.summary: Documents Erdős Problem #261: can every positive integer be represented as Σ k/2^k over a finite set S? Notes Part 1 (infinitely many) resolved by Cusick and Part 2 (all integers) remains open. Verified computationally for n ≤ 10000 by Tengely-Ulas-Zygadło. Imports Mathlib.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines recipPow2Weight(k) = k/2^k as a noncomputable rational function, recipPow2Sum as a Finset.sum of weights, IsRecipPow2Rep bundling |S| ≥ 2 with positivity and sum equality, and IsRepresentable as existential quantification over valid representations.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Proves elementary properties of the weight and sum functions: positivity (`recipPow2Weight_pos`), small values (1/2, 1/2, 3/8), `recipPow2Sum_empty`/`_singleton`/`_pair`, nonnegativity, the insert recurrence, and monotonicity under subset.

sections.title: Partial Sum Formula
sections.summary: `partial_sum_formula`: a closed form for the sum of weights over an initial segment, the key tool for the explicit representability constructions.

sections.title: Known Results
sections.summary: Proved (no axioms): explicit representability of small integers (`representable_one` through `representable_120` and `representable_le_7`), the Borwein–Loring family `borwein_loring_family` (n = 2^{m+1} − m − 2), and Cusick's infinitude theorem `cusick_infinitely_many` (for any N, some n ≥ N is representable).

sections.title: The Erdős Conjectures
sections.summary: `ErdosProblem261_infinitely_many`: Part 1 (resolved) — infinitely many n are representable, proved as a theorem (not axiomatized). Part 2 (every n ≥ 1 representable) remains open and is not asserted.

sections.title: Continuum Representations
sections.summary: Defines `IsInfiniteRep` for infinite sequences of distinct positive integers, but the definition omits the convergence condition Σ a(k)/2^{a(k)} = x (the docstrings flag this explicitly). As a result `ErdosProblem261_continuum` and `ErdosProblem261_two_reps` are trivially satisfiable placeholders — the continuum witness is a constant function of the index parameter t — and do not formalize Part 3 of the problem.

conclusion.summary: The formalization captures two of the three parts of Erdős Problem 261: the resolved infinitude question (Part 1, via Cusick's theorem) and the open universality conjecture (Part 2, all n ≥ 1, correctly left unformalized). The continuum representation question (Part 3) is stated as a Lean theorem but is only an honestly-flagged placeholder — `IsInfiniteRep` omits the convergence condition, so `ErdosProblem261_continuum`/`ErdosProblem261_two_reps` are trivially satisfiable and do not formalize Part 3. The 0-sorry, 0-axiom status reflects that all stated results (including Cusick's infinitude theorem and the Borwein–Loring family) are fully proved, with the Lean framework providing exact rational arithmetic for the weight function k/2^k. The full universality conjecture (Part 2) is not formalized.
conclusion.implications: Resolution of the universality conjecture would establish that the binary-weighted sum representation is a universal property of positive integers, connecting to the theory of complete sequences (every positive rational is representable as a subset sum). The continuum question would reveal whether representation spaces have the cardinality of the continuum, with implications for the combinatorial structure of binary partitions.
openQuestions: Does every positive integer n ≥ 1 admit a representation n/2^n = Σ k/2^k?
Does some rational admit continuum-many (2^ℵ₀) distinct infinite representations?
What is the minimal cardinality |S| needed for the representation of n as a function of n?
Can the Borwein–Loring family be extended to cover all n, or are there n requiring non-consecutive blocks?
